profile.title: Clumsy Bird
profile.goal: Fly through the gaps between pipes to increase your Steps without crashing.
profile.how_you_lose: Touch a pipe or the ground, or fly too high off the top of the screen.

controls.name: flap

mechanics.name: Get Ready delay
mechanics.detail: Play starts ~2s after entering; inputs before that don't move the bird.

mechanics.name: Scrolling pipes
mechanics.detail: Pairs of pipes move left at ~5 px/update; new pair spawns every 92 updates.

mechanics.name: Scoring
mechanics.detail: Passing a gap increments Steps and plays a sound.

mechanics.name: Ground collision
mechanics.detail: The ground scrolls at 4 px/update and is deadly on contact.

mechanics.name: Death and fall
mechanics.detail: On collision or flying too high, control ends and the bird falls before Game Over.

mechanics.name: Mute
mechanics.detail: Press M to toggle all audio.

profile.difficulty: Pipes move at -5 px/update (~300 px/s at 60 FPS). New pipes every 92 updates (~1.5 s). Effective gap ≈ 212 px (use center±106). Bird flap lifts ~72 px over 50 ms, gravity increases by 0.2 each update and rotation drifts down to +35°. Bird x is fixed at 60 px; ground top at viewport.height - 96.
profile.tips: Aim to keep the bird near the center of the next gap (next_gap_center_y). Tap early rather than late to counter rising gravity; one tap gives a quick ~72 px lift, so use short, spaced flaps. Start your climb before the gap reaches the bird’s x (use next_gap_left/right). Avoid riding too high—going above y = -80 triggers death. If sound is distracting, press M to mute.

rules.plan: Tap early to stay near the center of the next gap, tightening tolerance as it approaches. Emergency-flap near the ground and avoid flapping when near the top.

Keep gap-centering logic, but add a startup safety phase that taps more frequently for the first dozen frames to survive any Get Ready/input-lock, strengthen near-ground emergencies, and slightly reduce early cooldown. Maintain ceiling-avoidance and dynamic target banding near pipes.

Keep the solid gap-centering and early-game safety, but prevent last-second flaps from launching into the top pipe. Bias target slightly below gap center when close to pipes. Scale the near-ground bail-out so it only triggers when we’re genuinely low (and below center), and add a no-flap zone within ~26px of the gap’s top when close, except in true ground emergencies. Maintain ceiling avoidance and cooldown debouncing.

Keep the stable gap-centering and early safety but add stronger mouth-of-gap lip guards and a short no-flap window when arrival is imminent. Bias target further below center when close, lengthen cooldown near pipes, and use an estimated time-to-pipe from gap motion to suppress last-instant lifts that cause top-lip collisions. Retain ceiling avoidance and ground bailouts.

Keep the stable centering and lip guards, but add an early climb strategy when the next gap is far above: detect score-passage and big upward shift, start a short climb-boost with a lower cooldown and a tighter target band while still far from the pipes. Widen the early 'too low for next gap' bailout distance, and make cooldown dynamic (shorter when far/low, longer near the mouth). Preserve ceiling/ground safety and lip-guard suppression unless we’re clearly low.

Keep the stable gap-centering and mouth-of-gap lip guards, but add an explicit exit-guard right after a score: for a short window after passing a pipe, treat the just-passed gap’s bottom lip as dangerous and bail out sooner to prevent trailing-lip collisions. Track the last gap geometry on the frame before scoring to know that bottom lip, and flap if we descend too close while exiting. Do not change the next-gap targeting or ceiling/ground safeties, and keep the cooldown and time-to-pipe suppression for last-instant flaps.

profile.title: Clumsy Bird
profile.goal: Fly through as many gaps as possible to build your score.
profile.how_you_lose: You collide with a pipe or hit the ground.

controls.name: flap
controls.does: Makes the bird flap upward; also starts or restarts the run.

mechanics.name: Tap to flap against gravity
mechanics.detail: Each press briefly boosts the bird upward; no input makes it fall due to gravity.

mechanics.name: Pipes with gaps
mechanics.detail: Move horizontally and navigate through the openings; any collision ends the run.

mechanics.name: Score per gap
mechanics.detail: Passing a pipe pair increases the score by 1.

mechanics.name: Ground collision
mechanics.detail: Touching the ground immediately causes game over.

mechanics.name: New high score banner
mechanics.detail: A badge/notice appears when you beat your previous best.

profile.difficulty: Precise timing is required: the bird falls quickly under gravity, gaps are narrow, and any touch with pipes or the ground ends the run immediately.
profile.tips: Use light, rhythmic taps rather than big spikes; aim to enter each gap near its center; start your flap a bit before reaching a gap rather than reacting late; avoid holding input—single taps give finer control; stay calm after a near miss and reestablish your rhythm.

ends.cause: Hit the side of the first bottom pipe before the gap.
Hit the ground shortly after the run began (missed the initial rhythm).
Hit the ground right after the run began (didn’t gain altitude fast enough).
Clipped the first lower pipe while trying to enter the gap.

stalls.detail: no score change for 33s and the screen stopped changing

ui_confusion: Not totally clear when the run officially starts or when inputs stop counting after death; clearer on-screen feedback would help.
It’s not clear exactly when control/physics start after pressing start—taps before play began were ignored, and there’s no clear cue for when the bird becomes active.
It’s unclear whether the very first tap both starts the run and flaps, or if there’s any input buffering at the transition to ‘playing’.
I tapped a couple times before the run actually began; not clear when input starts counting toward flight.

learned: The bird drops immediately and fast; you need a steady tap rhythm right from the start to line up for the first gap.
The bird drops fast right from the start; you need to begin tapping immediately and keep a steady rhythm.
Pre-start taps don’t count; you need an immediate flap after the game actually starts to avoid dropping.
You need to flap immediately and then use short, timed taps; panic-mashing makes your height swing too much to line up with the gap.
Spamming taps near obstacles makes control sloppy; a steady rhythm works better to line up with gaps.
fun_moments: The brief scramble to line up with the first gap.
Feeling the quick lift from the first tap.
That first lift as the pipes scrolled in.
That brief rush as the first gap came into view.
Finding a quick tap cadence to climb toward the first gap.
frustrations: The run starts instantly with a pipe almost immediately, leaving little warm-up; a tiny grace period or more space before the first pipe would feel fairer.
Inputs tapped just before the run began were ignored, so the opening felt unforgiving without input buffering or a start-and-flap on the first tap.
The first obstacle appears almost immediately after the run starts, leaving very little time to stabilize.

verdict.headline: Snappy Flappy-style feel but punishing first seconds and unclear start cues kept all scores at 0.

clarity.why: 6 start retries ('pressed ['flap'] 2 times before play began' repeated) and 4 confusion notes about start timing, plus 'none in first run' for first point.

feedback.why: Inputs reacted 93% of the time (75/81 reacted_share 0.93), meeting the >=0.9 threshold.

challenge.why: Median survival 0.9s (vision) and 1.09s (overall) with 7 instant deaths in 0–5s; win_rate 0.0%.

skill_depth.why: Skilled vs random score ratio = 1.0 (skilled_avg_score 0 vs random_avg_score 0); vision APM 549.8 still avg_score 0.

learnability.why: Vision late vs early improvement flat (trend_per_run 0.0; early_avg 0, late_avg 0).

reward_cadence.why: Measured 5, but no points were ever earned (avg_score 0, best_score 0; 'never_seen: Score per gap'), so effective rewards were absent; lowering by 1.

variety.why: 43 distinct screens at 19.49 per minute and new screens in second half of longest run: 5.

fairness.why: All judged deaths were marked 'fair' (avoidable_share 1.0 over 4 deaths).

delivers_design.why: Only 'Mute toggle' and 'New high score banner' were seen; 'Pipes with gaps' and 'Score per gap' were never confirmed as seen.

observations: No one ever scored: avg_score 0, best_score 0, and 7 deaths at score 0.
Deaths were overwhelmingly immediate: 7 instant deaths occurred within 0–5 seconds; median survival was 0.9s (vision) and 1.09s (overall).

Start timing is unclear: 6 start retries were logged and 4 separate confusion notes explicitly cite uncertainty about when control begins (e.g., 'Pre-start taps don’t count; ... unclear whether the very first tap both starts the run and flaps').
High input spam did not help: vision actions_per_minute 549.8 with avg_survival 1.99s and avg_score 0 indicates mashing isn’t rewarded.
The first obstacle feels too close: multiple reflections say 'The first obstacle appears almost immediately... leaving very little time to stabilize.'
A stall occurred: run 4 (random) showed 'no score change for 33s and the screen stopped changing' with a 57.75s stall end.
Some inputs seemed ignored during transitions: 6/81 unresponsive checks (e.g., 'tap:Space' at t=48.63 and 50.88 had no reaction), matching player reports of pre-start taps not counting.

suggestions.change: Add a 1.0–1.5s delay or +250–400px extra spacing before the first pipe spawns on a fresh run.
suggestions.why: 7 deaths occurred within 0–5s and median survival was 0.9–1.09s; players report 'The first obstacle appears almost immediately... leaving very little time to stabilize.'

suggestions.change: Widen the first 3 pipe gaps by +10–20% (e.g., gapHeight *= 1.15 for the first three pairs).
suggestions.why: All runs ended at score 0 (avg_score 0, best_score 0) with repeated collisions at the first lower pipe; easing the opening should let new players reach their first point.

suggestions.change: Reduce gravity by ~10% (e.g., gravity from 0.6 to 0.54 per frame) and/or increase first-tap flap impulse by +5–8% (e.g., from -8.0 to -8.5 velocity) for the first second of a run.
suggestions.why: Multiple reflections: 'The bird drops immediately and fast'; early ground impacts happened within ~1s (two vision runs). A lighter opening curve addresses the 0–5s instant-death window.

suggestions.change: Make the first tap both start and flap; add a 150–200ms input buffer at the transition to 'playing'. Show a 'Tap to start'/'Get Ready' overlay that fades when control becomes active.
suggestions.why: 6 start retries and 4 confusion notes ('Pre-start taps don’t count'; 'not clear exactly when control/physics start'); unresponsive input checks around start confirm missed taps.

suggestions.change: Show a clear on-screen mute icon/state change when KeyM is pressed.
suggestions.why: KeyM taps at t=46.27, 55.83, 57.1 reacted false with 0.0 pixel change; a visible toggle reduces perceived unresponsiveness.

suggestions.change: Fix the stall condition that freezes play: ensure the game loop continues and entities update after death or pause; add a watchdog to reset if no world updates for >2s during 'playing'.
suggestions.why: Run 4 (random) stalled for 57.75s with 'no score change for 33s and the screen stopped changing.'

suggestions.change: Guarantee the first scorable pipe pair is reachable by moving its x-position further right (e.g., firstPipeX += 200px) and verify score increment on pass.
suggestions.why: No score events registered (avg_score 0; 'Score per gap' never seen); players could not reach a reward before dying.
